title: Assemble natural transitions and comparison from universal pairwise maps
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an open cover of $X$, $N_a$ a module on each chart $U_a$, and $p:Y\to X$ a morphism [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Write $W=U\times_XY$. Let $D$ be descent data of modules on the charts of $W$, and let $e_a:p_a^*N_a\simeq D_a$ be specified component isomorphisms [def-pc-local-overlap-transitions]. For every ordered pair $a,b$, give a map $\varphi_{ab}:\operatorname{pr}_1^*N_a\to\operatorname{pr}_2^*N_b$ on $U_a\times_XU_b$. Assume its canonical pullback to $W_a\times_YW_b$ commutes with the transition of $D$ under $\operatorname{pr}_1^*e_a$ and $\operatorname{pr}_2^*e_b$. Then there are natural overlap transitions $T$ on $U$ [def-pc-local-overlap-transitions], with $T_a=N_a$ literally, and an invertible component comparison between $p^*T$ and $D$, commuting on all test schemes. No finite-presentation, quasi-coherence, finiteness, directed-system, identity or cocycle assumptions are needed for the construction of $T$. The assumed square is solely on universal pairwise overlaps; its pullback uses the pseudofunctor composition comparisons as in overlapPairSquare [lem-pc-fp-overlap-pair-map-lifting].

proof.text: Construct the natural overlap transitions from universal pairwise maps with a generic pseudofunctor construction: use pullback.lift on every test object and pullHom on the corresponding pair map. The composite of a test arrow with the first lift equals the next lift by pullback.hom_ext. Mathlib pullHom_pullHom, followed by dependent simplification of that equality, proves naturality.

For a generic pseudofunctor, the universal-overlap value of the pulled transitions is the generic base-change formula by reflexivity. Factor any test pair through its universal pullback, pull back its assumed square, and use naturality of the two transition families and of mapComp' to prove Comparison.comm. The private assemblePairs theorem performs this generic construction and comparison proof. Specialize it to modulesPseudofunctor; overlapPairSquare is exactly the named specialization of its generic square, so no concrete sheaf pullback expansion is needed. The objects equal the supplied models literally; no diagonal or cocycle equations are imposed.

lean.statement: theorem exists_overlap_pair_transitions_comparison {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : X.OpenCover.{u}) (N : (a : U.I₀) → (U.X a).Modules) (p : Y ⟶ X) (D : modulesPseudofunctor.DescentData (U.pullback₁ p).f) (e : ∀ a, (Scheme.Modules.pullback (U.pullbackHom p a)).obj (N a) ≅ D.obj a) (φ : ∀ a b, (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (U.f a) (U.f b))).obj (N a) ⟶ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd (U.f a) (U.f b))).obj (N b)) (h : ∀ a b, overlapPairSquare U N p D e a b (φ a b)) : ∃ T : modulesPseudofunctor.OverlapTransitions U.f, (∀ a, T.obj a = N a) ∧ Nonempty ((T.pull (p := p) (α := fun a ↦ a) (fun a ↦ U.pullbackHom_map p a)).Comparison D)
